Notes from the observatory

The dome opens an hour after sunset, once the air inside has cooled to match the air outside. Until then there is nothing to do but wait, drink tea, and check the forecast for the third time.

Tonight the target is a faint galaxy 60 million light-years away 🌌. It will take four hours of exposure to see its spiral arms, & even then they will be barely there.

★ ★ ★

This sentence has no punctuation to speak of and simply keeps going for a very long time because the person writing it wanted to find out what happens when a single unbroken run of words stretches far past the length at which any reasonable reader would have expected a comma or a full stop to appear and yet none does so the reader is left to carry on reading without any hint of where a breath might be taken until at last after what feels like an age it finally stops

By morning the dome is closed again and the data is already on its way to the archive.
